### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §2.3.3, Definition 2.51, printed pp. 59–60 (PDF pp. 71–72), item `7sketches:2.3.3:def51` — the definition of a metric space by its four axioms (zero self-distance, separation, symmetry, the triangle inequality). That structure is exactly what this issue's category `Met` must carry before the completion can be built, so the definitional obligation is the same one and is not filed twice.

Seven Sketches immediately introduces a variant this issue does not scope: the EXTENDED metric space, whose distance takes values in the non-negative reals together with a point at infinity rather than in the reals. That variant is load-bearing for the book — its enrichment story recovers it exactly (a skeletal dagger Cost-category is an extended metric space), so it has to exist as a structure and not only as a remark — and this issue's current wording ("a rational- or real-valued distance") excludes it.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §2.3.3) the extended metric space: the same four axioms with the distance valued in `[0, ∞]`, together with a lemma identifying ordinary metric spaces among them as the ones whose distances are all finite

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §2.5.2, Proposition 2.96, printed p. 72 (PDF p. 84), item `7sketches:2.5.2:prop96` — all joins exist if and only if all meets do, proved by constructing the meet of a family as the join of its set of lower bounds. This is the same obligation as this issue's deferred remark from Definition 6.8, and its "and dually" clause already scopes both directions, so no separate issue is filed.

Two things the Seven Sketches statement asks for that this issue's checklist does not currently reach. First, it is stated for a PREORDER, not a poset: without antisymmetry a join is determined only up to the induced equivalence, so the construction has to produce an operation together with its universal property rather than a uniquely determined element, and the round trip between the two operations is an equivalence rather than an equality. Second, the book draws an immediate corollary that later sections use: a unital commutative quantale, whose definition requires only all joins, therefore has all meets — which is what makes the quantale-valued Hausdorff construction of Remark 2.97 well formed.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §2.5.2) the same equivalence for an arbitrary PREORDER: joins and meets given as operations with their universal properties, determined only up to the induced equivalence, with the meet constructed as the join of the set of lower bounds
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §2.5.2) the corollary that a structure required only to have all joins has all meets as well, in the form the quantale development consumes
